policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This guideline is explicitly non-binding ('not legally effective externally') and serves as guidance for applicants seeking approval for generative AI medical devices under the Digital Medical Products Act. It covers foundation models used within medical applications, excluding general-purpose foundation models not embedded in specific medical applications. Key focus areas include hallucination risk, inconsistency, data quality, and bias management. Post-market real-world evidence collection is recommended but not mandated.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document is a South Korean regulatory guideline for approving generative AI medical devices. Its central concern is ensuring patient safety and clinical validity of AI-generated outputs, including risks of hallucination, inconsistency, bias, and data quality failures. The governance rationale is framed primarily around protecting patients from unsafe medical AI outputs, requiring risk management processes, analytical performance validation, and clinical efficacy confirmation. Secondary framing around innovation enablement is present as the guideline aims to provide a workable approval pathway for novel GenAI medical devices. Fundamental rights appear as a minor frame through references to personal data protection.
